summary: Today’s pulse tracks Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg, US ambassador to Israel denounces West Bank settler attack on US photojournalist, and Multiple people killed as Canadian authorities tackle active blaze at Alberta military base. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are attack, israel, and mayor. In the background, Police investigate Reform mayor for allegedly sharing ‘naked and sexualised’ images of himself and French government in crisis talks after ‘colossal failure of the state’ keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
headlines.description: At least one person was killed in the strikes, which also hit a data centre used by Russia's equivalent of Facebook.

headlines.title: US ambassador to Israel denounces West Bank settler attack on US photojournalist
headlines.description: Mike Huckabee calls for arrest and prosecution of those responsible as Heidi Levine, 63, recovers in hospital in Israel The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced the settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror” and called for the arrest and prosecution of those responsible. Levine, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinian people attempting to harvest their olives in occupied West Bank towns.

headlines.title: Multiple people killed as Canadian authorities tackle active blaze at Alberta military base
headlines.description: Hospitals receive injured patients as doctor describes scale of emergency in Wainwright as a ‘disaster’ Multiple people have been killed and others injured after a deadly blaze tore through one of Canada’s busiest military training bases in Alberta, Canada’s defence minister said on Saturday. “I’m saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base,” said David McGuinty. The defence minister described the situation at CFB Wainwright as “active and delicate” with the fire being monitored very closely, telling reporters that high winds had worsened the fire.

headlines.title: Police investigate Reform mayor for allegedly sharing ‘naked and sexualised’ images of himself
headlines.description: Female colleague says she was forced out shortly after incident with Luke Campbell, Hull and East Yorkshire mayor A Reform UK mayor is under police investigation for allegedly showing “naked and sexualised” images of himself to a female member of staff. Luke Campbell, a former Olympic boxing champion and the mayor of Hull and East Yorkshire, is understood to have been questioned under caution by Humberside police earlier this month.

headlines.title: French government in crisis talks after ‘colossal failure of the state’
headlines.description: Ministers, officials and police under pressure over response to days of violent unrest in cities across France The French government was in crisis talks on Sunday after one of the most violent days of unrest in years left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted, and more than 2000 people arrested in cities across the country . Politicians on the left and right called for the resignation of the interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, after the government appeared to have been caught by surprise by the scale of violence as state buildings were stormed and torched, bus stops smashed, roads barricaded and shops broken into and destroyed.

headlines.title: Scholars conclude ‘beyond doubt’ that Shakespeare was main author of Edward III
headlines.description: Exclusive: Play anonymously published in 1596 was collaboration between Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, according to computer analysis Dramatic new evidence concludes that the play Edward III should be added to William Shakespeare’s canon, and also that it was a major collaboration with his contemporary rival Christopher Marlowe. The history was published anonymously in 1596, and it has long been thought that Shakespeare wrote at least a few scenes. However, Dr Rory Loughnane, a leading scholar and co-author of the research, told the Guardian that computerised textual analysis pushed the case “beyond any reasonable doubt” that the Stratford-born playwright was the principal writer.

headlinePool.title: Six-year-old among two dead after Kansas woman drives through soccer game, with 11 more injured
headlinePool.description: Wichita police say 34-year-old truck driver from Garden City was taken into custody amid case at youth soccer game The two people killed on Saturday when a truck drove through a youth soccer game in north-east Wichita, Kansas , were a six-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man, according to authorities. Eleven other people between the ages of five and 68 were injured in a case whose possible motivations remained unclear early on Sunday, by when it had captured attention across the US.

headlinePool.title: Arrests over France protests rise to 1,800, with whole streets in Paris ‘devastated’ – Europe live
headlinePool.description: Interior minister says ‘the Republic will not yield’ to France’s worst protests in years A dispatch here from Sam Jones, our reporter in Madrid, as protests have spread to Italy and Portugal The angry protests that have convulsed Spain and France in recent weeks have spilled over to Italy and Portugal , with rioters clashing with police and setting property on fire in Milan, and a tent encampment springing up in Lisbon over the weekend.

headlinePool.title: Manchester City owner’s £55m housing loan while Burnham was mayor investigated
headlinePool.description: Scrutiny committee looks into financing of Manchester Life project as PM promises ‘full transparency’ A £55m loan to Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi owner will be investigated as part of a review into a fund for housing projects while Andy Burnham was mayor. The prime minister has faced weeks of scrutiny over his links to Manchester City’s super-rich owners after the club was found guilty of boosting its income by £900m in a nine-year breach of financial rules.

headlinePool.title: Two killed and at least 17 injured as Russia and Ukraine trade blows on power infrastructure
headlinePool.description: Ukraine used more than 1,000 drones to target Russian oil depots, logistics facilities and datacentres Two people have been killed and at least 17 injured as Russia and Ukraine continue to trade strikes on each other’s power infrastructure, after the breakdown of Donald Trump’s short-lived and unilaterally declared “energy ceasefire”. One person was killed and 15 wounded overnight after Ukraine used more than 1,000 drones to target Russian oil depots, logistics facilities and datacentres in one of its largest ever aerial bombardments.

headlinePool.title: Air Force officer killed in rappelling accident before UTSA’s game against Navy
headlinePool.description: Officer fell from rafters during pregame display Man treated on field before being taken to hospital An Air Force officer has died after he fell from the rafters of the Alamodome before the University of Texas at San Antonio’s home game against Navy on Saturday. The officer, who has not been named, was taking part in an event to celebrate UTSA’s Salute to Armed Forces and Veterans night. He fell on to the field while rappelling down from the stadium rafters. He was treated on the field before being taken away on a stretcher. He later died from his injuries at a local hospital. Nellis Air Force Base said he was part of the 6th Combat Training Squadron. The unit helps train military members to rappel down from helicopters.

headlinePool.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
headlinePool.description: An expedition to a remote Pacific island hoping to uncover the American aviator's wreckage was on hold for three days.

headlinePool.title: Forget the seven-year itch: opposite-sex marriages more likely to end after two decades
headlinePool.description: ONS data for England and Wales shows 26% of heterosexual divorces in 2025 followed 20 years or more of marriage Most couples are aware of the dreaded “seven-year itch”, when the honeymoon period wears off and real life starts to bite. Now official data has shown that couples in England and Wales are more likely to split after 20 years. According to Office for National Statistics figures, more than a quarter of all divorces between opposite-sex couples happened after 20 years or longer of marriage.

headlinePool.title: Microsoft pulls out of AI datacentre project in Essex over power supply concerns
headlinePool.description: Development by UK firm Nscale heralded by ministers as largest of its kind in country loses anchor tenant The development of a huge AI datacentre hailed by the UK government has received a fresh setback after Microsoft pulled out of the project over concerns about power supplies. The development by the British company Nscale, heralded by ministers as the country’s largest AI datacentre when it was announced in 2025, was planned to open at Loughton in Essex next year.

headlinePool.title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery
headlinePool.description: Pope Leo XIV thanked thousands of faithful in St. Peter's Square on Sunday for their prayers while he was hospitalized, and said he plans to gradually return to his usual duties.
